findings.impact: Reusing the documented installation procedure could erase the wrong drive. Running the TPM example can target the wrong partition or fail. Ordinary nixos-rebuild does not repartition the disk; this is an installer/recovery hazard. Current root and boot declarations mount by /dev/mapper/crypted and /dev/disk/by-partlabel/ESP, not by this installer device string. The broken standalone Disko example may fail before touching disks; the wrong-drive risk becomes reachable when that separate recipe defect is fixed or bypassed.
findings.recommendation: Move each machine's installation device identity into its machine module using a verified /dev/disk/by-id path, retaining the reusable partition layout in x86_64.nix. Rewrite enrollment/recovery instructions to resolve the installed LUKS backing device rather than assume a numeric NVMe order. Require a human-readable model/size/serial verification before any destructive format in the documented procedure.
findings.validation: Compare lsblk/findmnt and stable by-id links on both physical hosts. Evaluate the resulting disko device paths and inspect generated scripts without executing them. No partitioning or enrollment operation was run in this review. Changing the declaration does not migrate data; retain current labels until a separately planned reinstall.

findings.title: Clipboard history persists more than its comment promises
findings.kind: Confirmed privacy tradeoff and misleading comment
findings.confidence: High for configuration; impact qualified below
findings.summary: cache-size = 10 means a 10 MiB read-time cache threshold (labeled MB in the schema) in installed Clipboard Indicator 71, not ten saved entries. history-size is 200. Its default cache-only-favorites is false, and the profile hides private mode, clearing and delete controls while leaving their shortcuts unbound. The active registry file is 309,225 bytes; its contents were not inspected. display-mode = 1 displays clipboard content in the panel, rather than an icon-only compact mode. findings.impact: Ordinary copied text can remain in a plaintext cache after clipboard replacement. Kitty copy-on-select broadens what enters the clipboard. findings.recommendation: Restore a reachable private-mode and clear-history control. Use icon-only display if previewing copied text is undesirable. Evaluate cache-only-favorites and application exclusions using the installed extension, then test persistence with harmless marker text; do not assume a configuration label guarantees every transient write is suppressed. Correct the cache-size units. If choosing to clear old history, do it explicitly through the extension after reviewing the retention decision. Lowering the cache threshold is not a deletion or complete retention policy.
findings.validation: Installed schema and registry/selection code were read; the extension is ACTIVE. File metadata only was collected. Validate using synthetic copied markers, a session restart and an application-exclusion test; no clipboard contents were read or changed during this review.

findings.title: Chrome explicitly bypasses the desktop secret store
findings.confidence: High for configuration; impact qualified below
findings.summary: The Chrome launcher forces --password-store=basic to avoid a keyring prompt, while this is a GNOME desktop. Chromium documents basic as its plaintext backend. A desktop keyring is not a complete defense against arbitrary code already running as the user.

Treat migrating an existing browser profile as a separate verified change rather than deleting credential files to silence prompts.

findings.title: Worktree-wide direnv trust also trusts future branch content
findings.summary: All .envrc files beneath the Herdr worktree directory are implicitly trusted. The configured worktree path is intentionally under the parent environment that supplies API credentials and sticky AWS context. This removes repeated setup prompts, but also means a changed or newly checked-out .envrc under that subtree executes without content-specific approval.

findings.impact: The trust boundary is every writer and branch that can supply an .envrc in that subtree. Git’s global ignore for .envrc does not prevent tracked or locally generated files from being evaluated.

cli_usage.source: Atuin SQLite history; read-only; no raw commands retained

Only recognized command names and allowlisted subcommand names were retained; arguments, private paths, queries, credentials and full history lines were never emitted.
These are retained history records, not an unbiased count of executions. Imports, sync, deduplication, suppression and missing sessions can change coverage.
Classification uses the leading shell command after simple wrappers. Commands later in pipelines and compound shell expressions are undercounted.
Nonzero exits were not equated with failures: Ctrl-C, grep/rg no-match and Terraform detailed-exitcode outcomes are examples.
Editor keystrokes, Herdr GUI actions, launchers, integrations and program-internal commands are not captured by leading-command history.

recommendations.title: Invest in the existing core workflow

recommendations.title: Keep directory navigation explicit while zoxide settles in

Keep cd semantics intact; use z for familiar destinations and zi for ambiguous interactive selection. The sample does not justify changing every cd into z.

recommendations.title: Choose one full Git UI if maintenance becomes costly
recommendations.detail: The setup provides command-line Git, Neogit, lazygit, Diffview and gitsigns. They have different roles, and shell history cannot measure Neovim UI use. Keep inline hunks and diff review; choose a preferred full Git UI only after trying the current options, rather than adding another one.

recommendations.title: Judge plugin performance with the actual slow action
recommendations.detail: There are 36 eager and 40 lazy plugin directories. A single isolated headless empty-buffer start reached its first screen at about 129 ms with no startup errors. This is not an interactive latency benchmark, but it does not support removing plugins simply because the count is high. Profile the specific scroll, completion or file-open interaction that feels slow.

recommendations.detail: Use Herdr for interactive agents and per-ticket workspaces. Keep OpenRig opt-in until one recurring task needs durable queues, ownership and bounded concurrency. Evaluate Paperclip on one measurable workflow before adding parallel orchestration state to the same task. Keep Agent Deck only if its tmux/session dashboard solves a separate need.

recommendations.title: Make ARC actions deterministic and recoverable
recommendations.detail: The ticket create/list/transition operations are structured API work. Consider a small typed client or a minimal MCP adapter with schema-validated output, idempotent issue creation, timeout/retry rules and a separate completion step. If retaining Claude, constrain its tool set and verify returned issue state.

recommendations.detail: ~/source/worktrees is automatically trusted by direnv, and ARC copies local permission grants then runs mise trust. This gives a fresh branch's environment code access to the parent source environment. Keep this only for repositories/branches whose contributors you trust; otherwise verify .envrc/mise changes before granting trust. This is an intentional convenience policy, not a confirmed incident.

system.scope: Independent read-only second pass over the system review, relevant repository modules, saved evaluation/runtime evidence, installed TLP source and Disko CLI source. No new approvals, evaluations, activations or hardware actions.
system.overall: The report is technically careful and most core findings are well-supported. The main corrections concern urgency and the distinction between an intentional policy, a future reinstall hazard, and a presently demonstrated failure. No finding requires merging the independent flakes or discarding the current working driver/power setup.

corrections.recommended_severity: P1 before reinstall; no current-boot emergency
corrections.change: Put the installer-only scope in the opening sentence and preferably the title: 'Installer targets a different NVMe device than the current system'. Ordinary rebuilds do not partition either drive. The saved evaluation explicitly uses /dev/mapper/crypted for root and /dev/disk/by-partlabel/ESP for /boot. Keep the recommendation to identify the intended install disk by stable identity; do not substitute /dev/nvme1n1 as another hard-coded fix.
evidence: nixos/profiles/x86_64.nix:41 fixes Disko's install device to /dev/nvme0n1.
/tmp/nix-review-system-eval.json reports rootDevice=/dev/mapper/crypted and bootMount=/dev/disk/by-partlabel/ESP for both hosts.
/tmp/nix-review-system-runtime.json reports active /boot on /dev/nvme1n1p1.
nixos/README.md:14 explicitly runs the destructive disko mode; lines 42–49 hard-code enrollment/wipe examples.
corrections.reason: The potential consequence of reusing the installer is severe, but the current configuration successfully mounts by mapper/label. A dashboard that presents this as an active wrong-root-disk failure would mislead. The current broken standalone Disko invocation may fail before touching disks, so the erase risk becomes reachable when that separate bootstrap defect is fixed or bypassed.

corrections.verdict: Root equivalence confirmed; reprioritize the intentional tradeoff
corrections.change: Treat this primarily as a trust-model and inaccurate-comment finding. Lead with retaining passwordless rebuild convenience while correctly acknowledging its root-equivalent authority; make changing authentication conditional on a different desired trust boundary. Do not prescribe a mandatory new password prompt, because passwordless updates are an explicit repo goal and the user has objected to additional approval interruptions.
evidence: nixos/profiles/shared.nix:57 and :61 allow unrestricted arguments for nixos-rebuild and nix with NOPASSWD.
nixos/profiles/shared.nix:37–48 documents passwordless updates as deliberate and describes sudo env as full root while implying the current commands are materially narrower.
Root AGENTS.md and home-manager/doc/AGENTS.md explicitly preserve the direct nixos-rebuild passwordless workflow.
corrections.reason: The security fact is correct: a user-selected Nix configuration or arbitrary command launched under root Nix already crosses the root boundary. This is not proof of compromise or an accidental configuration change. Also qualify the 600-minute cached sudo interval by its configured timestamp scope, commonly per terminal; do not imply every process automatically receives another terminal's cached authentication. A wrapper over user-writable configuration remains root-equivalent, correctly noted in the original finding.

corrections.verdict: Listener and authentication policy confirmed; qualify account-level inference
corrections.change: Describe the demonstrated state as 'SSH permits password-capable authentication on all interfaces'. Qualify that an actual password login also requires an unlocked account and applicable PAM policy, which were not inspected. Preserve the existing caveat that all-interface listening does not establish public-internet reachability. Say 'verify existing working authorized keys' rather than imply none exist merely because none are declaratively configured.
evidence: /tmp/nix-review-system-eval.json has PasswordAuthentication=true, KbdInteractiveAuthentication=true, sshOpenFirewall=true for both hosts.
/tmp/nix-review-system-runtime.json authentication section reports 0.0.0.0:22 and [::]:22.
Repository search found no declarative authorizedKeys or account password settings; imperative account/key state was not read.
corrections.reason: The exposed authentication policy is real and the recommendation is useful, but configured availability and a verified successful login are different evidence levels.

corrections.verdict: Boot observations confirmed; actual unlock protection remains unverified
corrections.change: Change kind from 'Confirmed protection gap' to 'Observed boot state; conditional TPM policy concern'. Keep the statement 'if the documented enrollment is in use' in the lead, not only the impact. bootctl's measured-UKI/OS flags do not establish that every relevant PCR is unmeasured, and crypttab tpm2-device=auto does not prove that an enrolled TPM slot exists or is used. Do not claim that LUKS is bypassed or the machine presently unlocks unattended.
evidence: nixos/profiles/x86_64.nix:65 requests TPM discovery during unlock.
nixos/README.md:44 documents PCRs 0+7 only.
/tmp/nix-review-system-runtime.json reports Secure Boot disabled/setup and measured UKI/OS false.
The audit explicitly did not read the enrolled LUKS token metadata or observe an unlock.
corrections.reason: The documented PCR choice does not authenticate an arbitrary substituted kernel/initrd under the observed unsigned-boot arrangement. The enrolled policy may differ, or the user may be entering a passphrase. The existing inspect-first, preserve-recovery-key recommendation is appropriate; Secure Boot/Lanzaboote should be a planned design choice, not an immediate blanket fix.

corrections.verdict: Confirmed against the deployed TLP version
corrections.change: Keep the unsupported NVME_APST findings. Clarify that /sys/module/nvme_core/parameters/default_ps_max_latency_us is a module default, not a direct readout of every drive's programmed APST table. When specifying stable DISK_DEVICES identifiers, use by-id basenames because TLP prepends /dev/disk/by-id/ itself.
evidence: A fresh recursive search of /nix/store/lkgryi8677g7qihdw0mcf6ma3vfi5km2-tlp-1.10.2 found no NVME_APST_* consumers.
Installed defaults.conf:23 declares DISK_DEVICES=nvme0n1 sda.

corrections.reason: The source-based no-op evidence is stronger than inferred power consumption. The AHCI-named helper really does cover NVMe in this installed release, so that part of the original report is valid rather than a mistaken SATA-only assumption.

Do not equate it with all USB-C ports, charging, or external displays being broken. Escalate to P2 if it repeats or affects the actual dock/display/charger workflow.

No connector, docking, charger, or alternate-mode functional test was performed.
corrections.reason: The failure message deserves investigation, but this audit has only one boot's evidence and no user-visible effect. The original recommendation to compare peripheral state and a known-good kernel is appropriately narrow.

confirmed_key_findings.detail: One derivation at a time does not bound one derivation's memory use. The recommendation to change cores only after observing OOMs respects the deliberate throughput choice and the lack of runtime evidence from the 2022 host.

report_wide_notes: Label P1 items by their trigger. The disk-layout issue is urgent before destructive installation, not evidence that a normal update will erase a drive.

A dry-run dependency plan is the repository's stated validation standard, but it is not a successful compile of all 47 planned derivations or an activation/hardware test. Preserve that qualification near any headline result.

Use observed, configured, inferred, and unverified consistently. Configuration availability alone does not establish successful password login, TPM auto-unlock, working backup restoration, or the practical impact of a boot warning.

Preserve explicit user goals: independent flakes, passwordless update convenience, separate manual firmware workflow, current driver experiments, and low-latency tuning. Recommendations should expose their costs and applicability rather than silently replacing those goals.
